title: How to Apply to Sawa as a Selling or Operating Agency: Application Guide
excerpt: Join Sawa with a Ministry licence, ETAA registration, insurance and references. No fee to join, 10% of the selling price, review in two to four business days.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

To join Sawa, an Egyptian travel company needs a Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration, passenger and liability insurance, a track record (two references or a portfolio) and a payout account. Apply through sawa.tours/verify and say whether you want to sell seats, operate departures, or both. There is no fee to join or list, and Sawa takes 10% of the selling price. You do not list your own tours: Sawa runs a fixed catalogue with its own calendar and prices, your agency sells seats on it, and approved operating agencies run departures they have travellers on. Review usually takes two to four business days.

The Egyptian Travel Agents Association provides an independent place to check agency membership.

Key facts

Fact Detail
Who can apply Egyptian travel companies with a Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration and passenger and liability insurance
Where to apply sawa.tours/verify, or WhatsApp +20 109 284 7613
What the application asks for Ministry licence, passenger and liability insurance, a track record (two references or a portfolio with review links) and a payout account
Roles Selling agency (sells seats), operating agency (runs departures under its own licence), or both
What you do not do Set your own tours, dates or prices. Sawa owns the catalogue, the calendar and the per-traveller price
Review time Usually two to four business days from a complete application, then an onboarding call
What review checks We check the documents and confirm the licence with the Ministry
Cost to join None. Sawa takes 10% of the selling price
Minimum to confirm a date Four travellers (people, not bookings); eight at most per departure

You hold the licence, the ETAA registration and the insurance, and you have bookings that never quite reach a viable group. This guide covers the paperwork between that position and a live place on Sawa: which documents to prepare, how to apply, how long review takes, and what you do once you are approved. It comes from the team behind Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure marketplace.

How do I join Sawa?

Apply through sawa.tours/verify with your Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration, insurance, track record and payout details, and tell Sawa which role you want: selling seats, operating departures, or both. The operators page explains the model before you apply.

The bar is the credentials. Only licensed Egyptian travel companies are approved. That is what lets every departure be run by a licensed operating company, and it protects licensed agencies from being undercut by operators with none. If you are unsure whether your credentials would pass, the routes in our guide to checking an Egypt tour company's licence are the same public routes travellers use.

One point is worth stating early. You do not list tours of your own. A shared departure is one date of a tour in Sawa's fixed catalogue, filled with travellers from several agencies. The destinations page shows where the catalogue runs. Your agency sells seats on those departures and earns a share of the pool for each seat sold, paid as set in the agency agreement. Calculations are in Egyptian pounds and payment is in euros. The operator of each departure is one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. An operating agency is entitled to its operating costs plus an agreed fee, and it also earns the pool share on the seats it sold itself.

The document checklist

Four things make up a complete application, alongside your ETAA registration.

Document What it is Why it matters
Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence Your company's licence to operate as a travel company in Egypt We confirm the licence with the Ministry
ETAA registration Your standing with the Egyptian Travel Agents Association, the chamber for travel companies Travellers can find you in the ETAA companies index at etaa-egypt.org
Passenger and liability insurance Cover for the travellers on your departures Required of every agency that operates departures
Track record Two references, or a portfolio of past tours with review links Shows the company has run tours before
Payout account Where your share is paid, in euros Needed before you can be paid

The licence and the ETAA registration are things the public can also check, so a completed application is both your entry to the platform and a traveller's reassurance that the departure is run by a real company.

How to apply, step by step

The application has five steps, and only one involves waiting.

  1. Check your eligibility. Confirm your Ministry licence is current, your ETAA registration stands and your insurance is in date. If one has lapsed, renew first; the review will find it either way.
  2. Gather the documents. Make sure your company's name matches across all of them, because the review compares them. Prepare your two references or your portfolio and review links, and your payout account details.
  3. Apply. Submit through sawa.tours/verify, or message Sawa on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613. Say whether you want to sell seats, operate departures, or both.
  4. Sawa reviews the application. Usually two to four business days. We check the documents and confirm the licence with the Ministry.
  5. Onboarding call, then live. After approval there is an onboarding call, and then you can sell seats on any departure. When you operate a departure, your company is named as the operating agency before the traveller deposit is due.

The review window

Review usually takes two to four business days from a complete application. An incomplete or mismatched application takes longer, because the review restarts on whatever was missing.

Newer agencies are welcome, but they must show references or a portfolio like everyone else. The track record does not have to be long, but it has to exist.

After approval: selling and operating

Approval opens both roles. As a selling agency you sell seats on the catalogue, and each seat earns a share of the pool. As an operating agency you run the day for the departures you operate: the vehicle, the guide and responsibility on the day are yours, and your company is named before the traveller deposit is due.

The traveller terms are the same on every day tour. Travellers reserve free, with no card. A date confirms, the GoAhead, when four travellers have reserved it. A 10% deposit is paid by payment link at the GoAhead, and the balance is due 2 days (48 hours) before departure. A forming date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and another date is suggested. Groups are capped at eight, and when a departure fills, a new independent departure opens. A traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded, and the tour still runs for the others. Cancelling at least 48 hours before departure is a full refund; under 48 hours means the 10% deposit is retained; force majeure is a full refund. A confirmed date is not cancelled for low numbers.

Packages and cruises run on longer terms: a 25% deposit at the GoAhead, the balance 14 days before, and four travellers needed by 30 days before. The full detail is on the terms page and the GoAhead promise.

Travellers pay by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros.

For an example of a live departure page, see the Aswan to Abu Simbel tour, from €50 per person, as listed in November 2026.

Tips and common mistakes

Tips for a clean application

  • Have your ETAA membership number to hand. It is what the public companies index shows, and the quickest thing for the review to match.
  • Keep names consistent across documents. A trading name on one and a legal name on another is the easiest way to slow a review.
  • Check the dates on your insurance. A certificate that is about to expire is the easiest avoidable delay.
  • Line up your references early. Two people who will answer a call, or a portfolio with working review links, saves days.
  • Decide your role before you apply. Selling seats needs no vehicles or guides; operating does.
  • Only operate departures you can staff. A confirmed date runs even if a traveller drops out, so a departure you operate is a commitment.

Mistakes that stall applications

  • Documents under different company names.
  • Expired or soon-to-expire insurance.
  • No references or portfolio.
  • Applying to operate without the guides and vehicles to do it.
  • Expecting to set your own dates or prices: the calendar and the per-traveller price are Sawa's.
  • Expecting approval to mean instant bookings: a date still needs four travellers, and that is the model working, not failing.

Who the application suits, and the honest limits

The application suits licensed agencies with bookings they cannot fill alone, smaller agencies without the marketing reach to fill a minibus, and seasonal businesses with quiet months.

The limits are worth reading before you apply. The catalogue and the calendar are Sawa's, so this is not a way to publish your own products. A place on the platform is a channel and not a guarantee of travellers: a date still has to reach four. Sawa takes 10% of the selling price. And operating a departure is a commitment to run it.

The short version

Joining Sawa takes a Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration, passenger and liability insurance, a track record and a payout account, applied for through sawa.tours/verify. There is no fee to join and Sawa takes 10% of the selling price. Review usually takes two to four business days, and you sell seats on, or operate, departures from a fixed catalogue rather than listing tours of your own. Gather the documents, choose your role, and apply, or message Sawa on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613.

About the author

Islam Hussein is an Egyptologist guide who has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, and the founder of Sawa Tours. Sawa Tours is operated by Online Era, registration 148500. More about Sawa Tours.

faq.q: Do I need insurance to join Sawa?
faq.a: Yes. Passenger and liability insurance is required, alongside the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence and ETAA registration.

faq.q: What does it cost to join?
faq.a: Nothing. There is no fee to join or list. Sawa takes 10% of the selling price.

faq.q: Can I list my own tours and dates?
faq.a: No. Sawa runs a fixed catalogue with its own calendar and prices. Your agency sells seats on those departures, and approved operating agencies run departures they have travellers on.
Yes. Newer agencies are welcome but must show references or a portfolio, along with a current licence, ETAA registration and insurance.

faq.q: When and how are agencies paid?
